smollm2.title: SmolLM2: When Smol Goes Big. Data-Centric Training of a Small Language Model

facts.small_model_data_sources: DCLM filtered with the FineWeb-Edu classifier (score 0 removed, scores 1 and 2 downsampled), FineWeb-Edu, Stack-Edu, InfiMM-WebMath, FineMath, Cosmopedia
facts.multilingual_data: none found; web data section is titled 'English web data' and math web data was filtered to retain only English content; no multilingual data or non-English language mentioned in fetched HTML
facts.stage2_mix_1_7b: 75% English web data (60/40 FineWeb-Edu to DCLM), 20% code, 5% math

quotes: data curation has an especially outsized influence for smaller models
we release both SmolLM2 as well as all datasets
applied fastText language classification to retain only English content
smollm2.notes: Base model for this post. 135M trained on 2T tokens with a 49,152 token tokenizer; the paper's web data section is explicitly 'English web data' and no multilingual data was found in the fetched text, which is why Hindi needs vocabulary extension and continued pretraining.

chinese_llama.title: Efficient and Effective Text Encoding for Chinese LLaMA and Alpaca

facts.pretrain_tokens: not stated in tokens, only GB

quotes: We extend LLaMA's existing vocabulary with an additional 20,000 Chinese tokens
the number of tokens generated by the Chinese LLaMA tokenizer is approximately half of those generated by the original LLaMA tokenizer
LoRA freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices.
chinese_llama.notes: The canonical recipe this post follows: add 20K target-language tokens, resize embeddings, continue pretraining with LoRA on attention and MLP, then instruction-tune. The corpus is stated in GB (20GB for 7B, 120GB for Plus), not in tokens.

swallow.title: Continual Pre-Training for Cross-Lingual LLM Adaptation: Enhancing Japanese Language Capabilities

facts.vocab_expansion_task_effect: no effect on most tasks; degrades automatic summarization (XL-Sum)
facts.cpt_english_share: 5% RefinedWeb, 5% English arXiv from The Pile
facts.ja_en_ratio_finding: 9:1 slightly outperformed 5:5 on average Japanese score
facts.gpus: NVIDIA A100 40GB, 8 per node, 32 nodes for 70B

quotes: Vocabulary expansion improved Japanese text generation efficiency up to 78%, due to a 56.2% token reduction in the Swallow Corpus.
Performance improves monotonically with Japanese training data up to 100B tokens without saturation.
Simply mixing parallel sentences enhances translation ability without harming other task performance.
swallow.notes: Evidence that vocabulary expansion buys efficiency at little accuracy cost, and that a 9:1 target:English mix with about 10% English replay works for continual pretraining of Llama 2.

ibrahim_cpt.title: Simple and Scalable Strategies to Continually Pre-train Large Language Models

facts.datasets: Pile 300B tokens, SlimPajama 300B tokens, German Common Crawl 200B tokens
facts.lr_finding: re-warming and re-decaying both necessary; infinite LR schedules avoid re-warming between tasks

quotes: A simple and scalable combination of learning rate re-warming, re-decaying, and replay is sufficient to match the performance of fully re-training.
Replay significantly reduces forgetting across both shifts, however, the stronger shift requires more replay.
even small amounts of replay are good at mitigating forgetting
ibrahim_cpt.notes: Justifies the recipe of re-warming the learning rate, decaying it again, and replaying 5% to 25% of the original English data during Hindi continued pretraining; a language shift is the strong-shift case.

focus.title: FOCUS: Effective Embedding Initialization for Monolingual Specialization of Multilingual Models

facts.idea: new target tokens initialized as sparse weighted combination of embeddings of overlapping tokens; weights from cosine similarity in fastText auxiliary embeddings with sparsemax
facts.languages: German, Arabic, Kiswahili, Hausa, isiXhosa, plus Scottish Gaelic, Luxembourgish, Cebuano, Samoan, Hmong

quotes: Additional target language tokens not present in the source model are represented as a linear combination of embeddings of semantically similar shared tokens.
Focus outperforms random initialization and previous work in language modeling and on a range of downstream tasks (NLI, QA, and NER).
focus.notes: The smarter alternative to mean-initializing new Hindi embeddings: express each new token as a combination of existing overlapping tokens. Gains over random init are large in loss (4.0 vs 24.0 MLM) and small in downstream accuracy.

wechsel.title: WECHSEL: Effective initialization of subword embeddings for cross-lingual transfer of monolingual language models

facts.idea: initialize target-language subword embeddings to be semantically similar to English ones using aligned multilingual static word embeddings
facts.languages: French, German, Chinese, Swahili; Sundanese, Scottish Gaelic, Uyghur, Malagasy

quotes: outperforms models of comparable size trained from scratch with up to 64x less training effort
WECHSEL can be applied to any model which uses subword-based tokenization and learns an embedding for each subword.
wechsel.notes: Shows how much of a small model is embeddings (about a third of GPT-2 small) and that good embedding initialization is worth orders of magnitude of training compute. Published at NAACL 2022; arXiv v1 December 2021.

deepseekmath.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

facts.grpo_no_critic: baseline estimated from group scores instead of a value model
facts.grpo_advantage: relative rewards of the outputs inside each group only
facts.grpo_kl: KL divergence to reference policy added directly to the loss, not to the reward

quotes: GRPO foregoes the critic model, instead estimating the baseline from group scores, significantly reducing training resources.
the advantage calculated based on relative rewards of the outputs inside each group only
GRPO regularizes by directly adding the KL divergence between the trained policy and the reference policy to the loss
deepseekmath.notes: Where GRPO comes from. Group of 64 samples per question, no value model, group-normalized advantages, KL to a reference in the loss; GRPO lifted a 7B model from 82.9 to 88.2 on GSM8K and 46.8 to 51.7 on MATH.

deepseek_r1.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

facts.r1_zero_training: pure RL (GRPO) on DeepSeek-V3-Base, no SFT
facts.cold_start_examples: thousands of long CoT examples before RL (exact count not stated)
facts.language_consistency_reward: proportion of target-language words in the CoT; Num(Words_target)/Num(Words)
facts.rule_based_rewards: accuracy reward (answer checked against reference or test cases) and format reward (<think> and </think> tags)

quotes: we bypass the conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) phase before RL training.
we collect thousands of cold-start data to fine-tune the DeepSeek-V3-Base as the starting point for RL
a language consistency reward during RL training, which is calculated as the proportion of target language words in the CoT
jumping from an initial 15.6% to an impressive 71.0%
deepseek_r1.notes: The template for RL with verifiable rewards at scale, including a language-consistency reward that directly maps to keeping a Hindi model answering in Hindi. arXiv v1 reports 15.6 to 71.0 AIME pass@1 (86.7 with majority voting); the current arXiv HTML (later revision) reports 77.9 pass@1 and cons@16 86.7.

instructgpt.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

facts.stages: SFT on demonstrations; reward model on comparisons; PPO against the reward model

quotes: outputs from the 1.3B parameter InstructGPT model are preferred to outputs from the 175B GPT-3, despite having 100x fewer parameters.
we hired a team of about 40 contractors on Upwork and through ScaleAI.
fine-tuning with human feedback is a promising direction for aligning language models with human intent.
instructgpt.notes: The original three-stage post-training pipeline (SFT, RM, PPO) with surprisingly small datasets: about 13k SFT prompts, 33k comparisons, 31k PPO prompts and about 40 labelers.

llama3.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models

facts.post_training_per_round: collect preference annotations and SFT data, sample synthetic data from the latest models, SFT then DPO
facts.pretrain_mix: 50% general knowledge, 25% mathematical and reasoning, 17% code, 8% multilingual
facts.vocab_composition: 100K tiktoken tokens plus 28K additional tokens for non-English languages
facts.dpo_vs_ppo: DPO required less compute and performed better, especially on IFEval
facts.rejection_sampling_note: rejection sampling is part of the brief but the phrase was not in the fetched sentences

quotes: Following Llama 2, we apply the above methods in six rounds.
roughly 50% of tokens corresponding to general knowledge, 25% of mathematical and reasoning tokens, 17% code tokens, and 8% multilingual tokens
We pre-train Llama 3 on a corpus of about 15T multilingual tokens.
llama3.notes: How a large lab does the same pipeline at scale: 15.6T tokens on up to 16K H100s with only 8% multilingual data, then six rounds of rejection sampling, SFT and DPO. Meta also extended its vocabulary by 28K tokens for non-English text.

tulu3.title: Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training

facts.rlvr_definition: RL objective for skills with verifiable answers; a constant reward is given only when the completion is verified correct, no learned reward model
facts.stages: data curation, SFT, preference tuning (DPO), RLVR

quotes: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)
only provide rewards when the model's generations are verified to be correct
obtains a constant reward value if a completion is successful
tulu3.notes: Names and defines RLVR: replace the reward model with a verifier on math and instruction-following prompts. The exact reward constant, RL algorithm, and isolated RLVR gains were not recoverable from the fetched HTML.

constitutional_ai.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

facts.rlaif: AI evaluates which of two samples is better according to constitutional principles; a preference model is trained on those AI preferences and used as the RL reward
facts.supervised_phase: generate response, critique it against a principle, revise, fine-tune on revisions
facts.human_labels: human labels for helpfulness, AI labels only for harmlessness

quotes: we use human labels for helpfulness, but only AI labels for harmlessness.
We have written a total of 16 different principles related to harmlessness.
Constitutional AI makes it possible to control AI behavior more precisely with far fewer human labels.
constitutional_ai.notes: Anthropic's variant of the pipeline: the reward signal for harmlessness comes from an AI judge applying written principles (RLAIF) rather than from human comparisons.

fineweb2.title: FineWeb2: One Pipeline to Scale Them All. Adapting Pre-Training Data Processing to Every Language

facts.hindi_subset_id: hin_Deva (config confirmed via datasets-server size endpoint)

quotes: Hand-designing a different pipeline for each language does not scale.
Our pipeline can be automatically adapted based on language-specific statistics.
Released under the permissive ODC-By License
fineweb2.notes: The source of the Hindi pretraining text: 20 TB, about 5 billion documents across 1,868 language-script pairs from 96 Common Crawl snapshots, ODC-By licensed. The hin_Deva config holds 22,151,227 rows (22.1M train, 55K test) in 34.4 GB of parquet per the HF datasets-server size endpoint; a token count is not stated.

sarvam1.title: Sarvam 1: The first Indian language LLM

facts.languages: 10 Indic (Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Oriya, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu) plus English
facts.fertility_other_models: 4 to 8 (per press coverage of the blog)
facts.tokenizer_efficiency_claim: 2-4x more efficient than existing multilingual models
facts.hardware: 1,024 HGX H100 GPUs on Yotta Shakti cluster
facts.benchmark_claim: best in class vs Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.2-3B; competitive against Llama-3.1-8B
facts.inference_speed_claim: 4-6x faster inference compared to larger models
facts.source_note: blog returned HTTP 403; facts taken from the Hugging Face model card https://huggingface.co/sarvamai/sarvam-1 and search snippets of press coverage

quotes: 2-billion parameter language model specifically optimized for Indian languages
Achieves fertility rates of 1.4-2.1 across all supported languages
4-6x faster inference compared to larger models
sarvam1.notes: An Indian lab doing the whole pipeline from scratch rather than adapting: a 2B model with a purpose-built tokenizer (1.4 to 2.1 tokens per Indic word) trained on 1,024 H100s. The claimed wins are against 2B-3B models, with parity claimed against Llama-3.1-8B.

openhathi.title: Announcing OpenHathi Series

facts.vocab_added: 16K Hindi SentencePiece tokens merged into the 32K Llama-2 vocabulary (per search snippets; blog returned 403)
facts.training_phases: phase 1 embedding alignment for Hindi embeddings; phase 2 bilingual language modelling (per search snippets)

quotes: This is a 7B parameter, based on Llama2, trained on Hindi, English, and Hinglish.
This is a base model and not meant to be used as is.
openhathi.notes: The first open Hindi adaptation of Llama-2 with an extended tokenizer and a two-phase training scheme. The blog itself could not be fetched; the vocabulary and phase details come from secondary reporting and should be cited cautiously.

airavata.title: Airavata: Introducing Hindi Instruction-tuned LLM

facts.lora_targets: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj
facts.indicinstruct_sources: FLAN-v2, Anthropic-HHH, Dolly, OpenAssistant, LMSYS-Chat, WikiHow, Anudesh
facts.translation_filter: translated examples kept only if chrF++ of back-translation vs English is 50 or above
facts.vs_openhathi: significantly outperforms OpenHathi on most NLU tasks
facts.vs_gpt4: still trails significantly behind GPT-4 in human evaluation

quotes: We perform parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA
The performance in Indian languages is considerably behind that of English.
This model is designed for research purposes and is not recommended for any production use-cases.
airavata.notes: The Hindi SFT precedent: OpenHathi plus LoRA on about 385k mostly machine-translated instructions, filtered by back-translation chrF++. It is also where the IndicSentiment evaluation used in this post appears as a benchmark.

indicxtreme.title: Towards Leaving No Indic Language Behind: Building Monolingual Corpora, Benchmark and Models for Indic Languages (IndicXTREME)

facts.indicsentiment_source: synthetic product reviews written by annotators in English, then manually translated

quotes: All the reviews are first written in English and then manually translated to 13 Indic languages.
We ask annotators to create synthetic reviews for real products.
indicxtreme.notes: Defines the IndicSentiment dataset used as the verifiable-reward task: human-written English product reviews translated into Indic languages, with a 156-example dev set and 1000-example test set. Published at ACL 2023; arXiv v1 December 2022.

gemma3.title: Gemma 3 Technical Report

facts.tokenizer: same as Gemini 2.0, SentencePiece, split digits, preserved whitespace, byte-level encodings
facts.multilingual: increased monolingual and parallel multilingual data; no language count given

quotes: We use the same tokenizer as Gemini 2.0: a SentencePiece tokenizer with split digits, preserved whitespace, and byte-level encodings.
All Gemma 3 models are trained with knowledge distillation.
gemma3.notes: Example of a large vocabulary (about 256k to 262k entries) inherited from Gemini, which is why Gemma tokenizes Hindi far more efficiently than a 49k English tokenizer.

qwen25.title: Qwen2.5 Technical Report

facts.languages: no explicit language list or count in fetched text; Hindi not mentioned

quotes: a vocabulary of 151,643 regular tokens
18 trillion tokens
qwen25.notes: Another large-vocabulary, large-token-budget model whose post-training pipeline (SFT, DPO, GRPO) mirrors the small-scale pipeline in this post. Hindi support could not be confirmed from the fetched report.

trl_grpo.title: TRL GRPOTrainer documentation

facts.advantage: (r_i - mean(r)) / std(r) within the group of G completions
facts.reward_func_inputs: prompts, completions, completion_ids, trainer_state, plus any dataset columns as kwargs
facts.reward_func_output: list of floats, one per completion
facts.loss_type_options: grpo, dapo, dr_grpo, sapo, cispo, vespo
facts.beta_note: docs state beta = 0.0 by default so the KL divergence term is not used, unlike DeepSeekMath

quotes: The function must return a list of floats. Each float represents the reward corresponding to a single completion.
GRPO is an online learning algorithm, meaning it improves iteratively by using the data generated by the trained model itself during training.
trl_grpo.notes: The implementation used in this post. Defaults differ from the DeepSeekMath paper: 8 generations per prompt, DAPO-style loss, and no KL term (beta 0.0) unless set.

facts.indic_premium: close to a 5x increase in cost for mid-resourced Indic languages with non-Latin scripts

Speakers of a large number of the supported languages are overcharged while obtaining poorer results.
